source_name: Code4rena Monetrix Findings and Analysis Report (2026-04)
finding_title: PM borrow liabilities are omitted from backing, allowing phantom surplus settlement
summary: Monetrix credited Portfolio Margin supplied balances from the HyperCore 0x811 precompile as positive backing but did not subtract borrow liabilities from the same PM/Borrow-Lend state. The resulting totalBackingSigned(), surplus(), and distributableSurplus() could be overstated, allowing normal settlement to distribute phantom yield even when true PM net equity was negative.
root_cause: external PM/Borrow-Lend account valuation used gross supplied assets as backing while ignoring sibling borrow liability fields, so settlement safety gates consumed gross collateral instead of net external equity
broken_invariants: external strategy or PM account backing must be measured as net equity, not gross supplied assets only
every liability field in an upstream account state that can reduce claimable backing must be subtracted before surplus gates authorize yield
settlement gates must not distribute yield when a positive supplied balance is offset by larger borrow debt in the same external account
attack_preconditions: the vault or configured L1 account has registered PM/Borrow-Lend supplied slots that feed totalBackingSigned()
the external PM account can carry borrow liabilities while still reporting supplied balances
settlement is initialized and a normal settle() call evaluates distributableSurplus() from the supply-only PM reader
attacker_capability: ordinary yield recipient or protocol participant can benefit from phantom yield once normal settlement accepts overstated backing; the core bug is the contract-side safety gate omitting liabilities, not malicious Operator parameter selection
trigger_actions: enter or observe a PM state with supplied assets and borrow liabilities
call or wait for normal settlement that computes totalBackingSigned() from suppliedBalance()
distribute accepted yield through the vault's yield path

impact.description: Phantom distributable surplus can mint USDM into sUSDM and route USDC to configured recipients while true PM liabilities exceed real backing. The final report classified the issue as Medium because the damage is bounded by settlement cadence and APR caps but the safety gate can accept false surplus.

why_not_higher: final C4 severity is Medium; the exploit depends on PM borrow state and accepted settlement windows, and per-window yield is bounded by annualized APR and protocol configuration
why_not_lower: the finding is included in the final C4 report as the only Medium; it affects value-moving settlement gates and can convert external-accounting overstatement into real yield distribution
common_false_positive_angles: do not treat this as mere Operator misreporting if on-chain gates are supposed to independently bound settlement by backing
verify the upstream reader really exposes liability fields or net-equity data; if the queried API/precompile is supply-only by design and another reader subtracts debt, the pattern may not apply
confirm the credited external balance feeds a value-moving gate, not only an informational UI metric
mitigations: Decode and account for both PM supply and PM borrow state. Replace supply-only readers with a full PM state reader or a reliable net-equity source, and subtract borrow liabilities in the same units and valuation framework before computing totalBackingSigned(), surplus(), or distributableSurplus().

snippets.note: suppliedBalance decodes only the supplied field from the 0x811 response
suppliedUsdcEvm inherits the supply-only PM blind spot
suppliedNotionalUsdcFromPerp values supplied non-USDC balances without borrow offset
_readL1Backing adds PM supplied values as positive backing
surplus and distributableSurplus consume inflated totalBackingSigned
settleDailyPnL Gate 3 accepts distributableSurplus before phantom yield can be settled
